title: Orbital reclaimer: fragmentation-aware eviction and occupancy-driven kernel routing
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We observe tail-latency spikes and suboptimal GPU occupancy in mixed-tenancy workloads caused by highly fragmented KV residency and mismatch between fragment shapes and kernel microvariants. Current eviction heuristics treat fragments uniformly which leads to repeated decode stalls for long-running streams and poor kernel utilization for microfragments.

Proposal: Implement an 'Orbital Reclaimer' — a fragmentation-aware eviction manager that assigns fragments to residency bands (orbitals) based on access frequency, fragment shape, and decode-phase heat. Paired with an occupancy-driven kernel router that selects microkernel implementations based on observed fragment sizes and current hardware occupancy, this aims to: reduce decode stalls, improve kernel SIMD utilization, and lower per-token cost under bursty traffic.

Scope: prototype eviction bands, lightweight fragment fingerprinting, kernel-routing heuristic, simulator, unit and perf tests, and a canary rollout on dedicated pools. This ticket covers design, simulator results, initial runtime integration, and monitoring dashboards required for rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator shows >=15% reduction in decode stall events for mixed short+long workloads compared to baseline eviction
End-to-end 95th percentile latency improved by >=10% on the dedicated canary pool under our benchmark profile
Kernel occupancy (SM utilization) increases by >=8% for microfragment-heavy workloads without regressing large-sequence throughput
Eviction decisions annotated in traces and visible in Console dashboard with per-tenant orbital assignments
Feature flags and default fallbacks in place; safe rollback within one hour of rollout
notes: Design choice: use lightweight fingerprint (8B) aggregated with LRU counters to avoid per-fragment heavy metadata. Trade-off: slightly less precise hot-path detection in exchange for lower memory overhead.

Eviction bands: HOT (resident, no reclaim), WARM (evictable with quick refill), ORBITAL (aged fragments, batched eviction candidates). Orbitals chosen to bias eviction away from fragments that compose prefix chains frequently accessed together.
Kernel routing: map fragment length buckets (<=128, 129-512, >512 tokens) to microkernel variants and adaptively bias based on measured SM occupancy in the last 100ms window.
Safety: when occupancy data is noisy, fall back to static selection per model-size profile. Feature gated behind runtime flag runtime.eviction.orbital and runtime.kernel.router.automatic
Experiment plan: A/B with 10% traffic on a dedicated pool, extend to 30% if 1-week metrics show no regressions. Target full rollout after two cycles of feedback and improved dashboards.

Monitoring: add metrics: orbital_assignment_count, orbital_evictions_per_min, kernel_switch_rate, decode_stall_events, sm_occupancy_percentile. Dashboards staged under Console -> Runtime -> KV Orbits.
Long-term: consider cross-tenant cooperative reclamation where tenants with flexible SLOs donate residency credits (future ticket).
